Name of the Complainant : Sh. A.K. Singh, Food Inspector Offence complained of or proved : Section 2 (ix) (K) of the   1954 r/w Rule 42 of PFA Rules, 1955  Da vs . Prem Chand Page 1/9 on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4165112/

Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : Acquitted.
Arguments heard on : 12.02.2016 Judgment announced on : 12.02.2016

Brief facts of the case :
1

In brief, the case of the prosecution is that on 26.12.2005 at about 7.15 p.m, 
Food Inspector A.K. Singh and Field Assistant Ashok Kumar under the supervision and directions of SDM/LHA Sh. Vishwendra visited the premises of M/s Garg Store, where accused Prem Chand who was the vendorcumproprietor was found present conducting the business of food articles including the sale of Gutkha, for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the PFA Act & PFA Rules) the Food Inspector collected/ purchased the sample of Gutkha.

2 During the course of investigation, it was revealed that Sh. Prem Chand S/o Late Sh. Kali Ram Gupta was the vendorcumproprietor of M/s Garg Store, who was also the Incharge and responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.

3 It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was misbranded because language of statutory warning is not as per the language of Rule 42 of PFA Act.

Accordingly, after obtaining the necessary Sanction/ Consent under Section 20 of the PFA Act, the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of section 2 (ix) (K) of the PFA Act r/w Rule 42 of PFA Rules which is punishable under section 16 (1) (a) read with Sec. 7 of the PFA Act, 1954.

4 After the complaint was filed, the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.06.2006.
5

Notice for violation of provisions of section 2 (ix) (k) of the PFA Act r/w Rule 42 of PFA Rules which is punishable under section 16 (1) (a) read with Sec. 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 was framed against the accused vide order dated 14.01.2010 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
6 Statements of the accused persons U/sec. 313 Cr. P.C. were recorded on 17.04.2013 wherein the accused persons claimed themselves to be innocent.
Despite opportunity, accused persons did not lead any defence evidence.

A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under:
Da vs . Prem Chand Page 1/9 on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4165112/
2 7 PW1 Sh. Vishwendra, deposed that on 26.12.2005 when he was posted as SDM/LHA Vasant Vihar, under his direction and supervision, FI A.K. Singh and FA Ashok Kumar visited the premises of M/s. Garg Store, Shop No. 16, Moti Bagh, New Delhi, where accused Prem Chand present in the Court was found conducting the business of food articles stored there for sale ready for sale for human consumption including Gutkha in original sealed poly packets bearing identical label declaration.
He deposed that they disclosed their identity and intention for purchasing of Gutkha (ready for sale), for analysis to which accused agreed.

He deposed that before purchasing the sample, FI A.K.
Singh tried his best to procure and neighbouring shopkeepers but as none agreed and on his request, FA Ashok Kumar agreed and joined as a witness.

He deposed that at about 7.15 pm FI A.K.
Singh purchased 9 x 58 pouches i.e. 9 sealed packets of Gutkha, each packet containing 58 pouches baring identical label declaration, Dilbagh Brand on payment of Rs. 405/ vide vendor's receipt Ex.PW1/A.

He deposed that then FI A.K. Singh divided the sample into three equal parts by putting three originally sealed packets in one counterpart and each counterpart containing the sample of Gutkha was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.

He deposed that notice in Form VI Ex.PW1/B was prepared and the label was reproduced in Form VI and a copy of was given to accused as per his endorsement at point A to A bearing his signature at point A.
He deposed that Vendor made endorsement that he purchased the sample packets from M/s. Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd. B.J. Road Industrial Area, Ghaziabad, UP.
Accordingly, a notice under section 14A Ex.PW1/D addressing to M/s.
Som Fresheners
Pvt . Ltd
B.J. Road Industrial Area Ghaziabad, UP was also prepared at the spot.
Then the Panchnama Ex.PW1/C was prepared.
Report under Rule 9 (e) Ex.PW1/C1 was also prepared at the spot.

He deposed that the remaining two counterparts of sample in intact condition alongwith two copies of Memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with him on 27.12.2005 i.e. next working day vide receipt Ex.PW1/E bearing his signature at point A and that of FI at point B which he identify, with the intimation that one counterpart of the sample in intact condition was already been deposited with the PA.
All the copies of Memo of Form VII were marked with the impression of seal which was used to seal the sample counterparts.
PA receipt is Ex.PW1/F.

He deposed that on receipt of PA Report Ex.PW1/G,
according to which the sample was found misbranded as statutory warning was not as per Rule 42 of PFA Rules, as mentioned therein in portion X.

He deposed that after completion of the investigation by FI, the complete case file alongwith all the statutory documents were sent to the Director Sh. K.S.
Wahi through him, who after going through the entire case file, applied his mind and gave the sanction for prosecution Ex.PW1/H against the accused persons.
He deposed that he identifies the signature of Sh. K.S. Wahi at point A on Ex.PW1/H, being conversant with his writing and signatures during his official course of duties.
8 During his crossexamination by accused no. 1, he admitted that sample packets were in originally sealed condition and were not tempered with in any manner.
He stated that the vendor did not give the copy of Bill at the spot but made an endorsement that he purchased the sample commodity from M/s. Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd.
He admitted that after investigation that the sample commodity was manufactured and supplied by M/s. Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd.
He denied that the sanction against the accused no. 1 was granted wrongly.
He admitted that the label of the sample packets was reproduced by the FI on the Notice in Form VI.
He denied that there was no violation of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.

Da vs . Prem Chand Page 1/9 on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4165112/
3 9
During his crossexamination by accused no. 2 & 3, he stated that he did not accompany the FI to the factory of the accused no. 3 during investigation.
He stated that he was satisfied by the report of the FI.
He stated that he does not remember that FI visited the factory during investigation.
He denied that accused no. 2 & 3 have been falsely implicated.
10 PW2
Sh. Ashok Kumar, Field Assistant, deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW1 in his examination in chief.
11 During his crossexamination by accused no. 1, he stated that there were approx. 2025 poly packets of sample commodity available with the vendor at that time.
He admitted that the sample commodity was found in original sealed condition.
He admitted that the label declaration of the sample commodity was reproduced by FI on Notice in Form VI i.e. on Ex.PW1/B.
He admitted that no leakage, breakage or tampering was noticed in the sample commodity at the time of lifting the sample.
He admitted that the vendor was not the manufacture of sample commodity.
12 During his crossexamination by accused no. 2 and 3, he stated that vendor had not shown any Bill of purchase of the sample commodity to the FI at the spot.
He admitted that in this case a sample of Gutkha (Dilbagh Brand) was lifted by the FI.
He stated that the sample of Supari or Chewing Tobacco was not lifted by the FI at the spot.
He stated that the he does not know if Gutkha contains Supari and Tobacco.

He stated that he cannot comment if the meaning of words, "Chewing, Supari and Tobacco is injurious to health" and the words, "Chewing, Supari is injurious to health" and the words "Chewing, Tobacco is injurious to health", is one and the same.
13
PW3, Shri A.K. Singh, FSO, deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW1 in his examination in chief.
14 During his crossexamination by accused no. 1, he admitted that the sample packets were in original sealed condition and were not tampered with in any manner.

He stated that the vendor did not supply copy of the bill of purchase even during the investigation despite his request several time but as per the label declaration, the sample commodity was manufactured by SOM Freshner Pvt.
Ltd., hence, the SOM Freshner Pvt. Ltd. has been impleaded as an accused in this case.

15 During his crossexamination by accused no. 2 & 3, he admitted that meaning of words, "Chewing, Supari and Tobacco is injurious to health", and the words, "Chewing, Supari is injurious to health" and the words "Chewing, Tobacco is injurious to health", is one and the same but added that there is violation of the relevant PFA Rules.
16 This so far is the evidence in the matter.
17 I have carefully considered the submissions of both sides and perused the record meticulously.
18 The accused persons are facing the allegations of violating the provision provided under section 2 (ix) (k) of the PFA Act for contravening Rule 42 of PFA Rules .

As per the report of Public Analyst ,
the sample of "Gutkha" was misbranded because statutory warning was not given thereon as per the language of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.
Accused no. 1 is the Vendor of sample commodity and the accused no. 3 is the Manufacturer of which the accused no. 4 is the Nominee.

19 The star / the material Da vs . Prem Chand Page 1/9 on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4165112/
4 witness of the prosecution i.e. Food Inspector Sh. A K Singh proved the sample proceedings dated 26.12.2005 as were conducted in the presence of SDM/LHA.

From the deposition of the prosecution witnesses who duly corroborated each other coupled with documents Ex. PW1/ A to C i.e. Vendor's receipt, Notice Form VI and panchnama as proved by the prosecution, the admissions made by the accused persons during their examination under Section 313 Cr. P.C. as recorded before the Ld.
Predecessor of this Court on 17.04.2013 which are admissible in evidence against the accused persons in view of sub clause (4) of Section 313 Cr. P C, no doubt remains that the sample of Gutkha was indeed collected by the Food Inspector for analysis from premises of M/s Garg store of which accused Prem Chand is the vendor and incharge of and responsible for conduct of day to day business of the above said M/s. Garg Store.
The procedural formality for lifting the sample were also duly adhere to as reflected from the testimony of prosecution witnesses.
20 Section 2 (ix) reads to the effect that 'an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded if it is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this act or Rules made thereunder'.

The article in question is a 'Gutkha'; the sample of which was adjudged positive for Nicotine test and was also having therein 'betel nut' as an ingredient, meaning thereby that it was a tobacco product containing supari/betel nut as well.
A sample of the given article in respect of its labelrequirements is required to be adjudged in the light of the Provision under Rule 42 (zzz) & (zzz) (6).

These provisions are being reproduced hereunder:
Rule 42 (zzz) [ " Every package of chewing tobacco shall bear the following label,
namelyChewing of tobacco is injurious to health".] Rule 42 (zzz) (6) [" Every packages of supari and advertisement relating thereto shall carry the following warning in conspicuous and bold print namely - Chewing of Supari is Injurious to Health"]
21 It is important to note that no standard of Gutkha is prescribed under the PFA Act and the PFA Rules.
The Report Ex. PW1/F and the Notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B both do bear the reproduction of the label declaration drawn from the sealed Gutkha pouches.
The said label declaration does contain the statutory warning to the effect that 'chewing of tobacco and supari is injurious to health'.
The prosecution has in no way been able to establish as to how and why the declaration on the label of the sample commodity was violative of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.
The PFA Rules in general and Rule 42 in particular, are entirely silent as to the language which is to be used if, both Tobacco and Supari are the ingredients of a particular food article.

It nowhere specifies as to whether in that situation,
the statutory warning as under Rule 42 (ZZZ) and Rule 42 (ZZZ) (6) are to be written separately or the warning is to be expressed in a single sentence combining the warning prescribed under Rule 42 (ZZZ) and Rule 42 (ZZZ) (6), as is done in the present case.
I am of the opinion that either way, the same meaning would be conveyed.
It is to be borne in mind that the purpose of prescribing labelling condition under PFA Act and Rules is to empower the consumer to take informed decision.

The consumer in no way is prejudiced by the warning given by the accused persons on the label of sample commodity as same meaning is conveyed that chewing of Supari as well as Tobacco is injurious to health.
So the accused persons are not found guilty of contravening section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act and Rule 42 of PFA Rules, and stand acquitted.

Present: Ld. SPP for the complainant. 
 All Accused in person with Ld. Counsel.

Vide separate judgment announced in the open Court today, all the accused persons are acquitted for the offence punishable under section 16(1) (a) r/w section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 for violation of section 2 (ix) (k) r/w Rule 42 of the PFA Act.
File be consigned to Record Room after furnishing of Bail Bond U/Sec. 437A Cr.PC to be furnished within one month from today.
[Priya Mahendra] ACMMII/PHC/ND/12.02.2016
